title: L'arrivée
brief: You've just landed in Paris. You're outside the terminal with a suitcase, and a taxi driver is looking at you.

visit.brief: Get in the taxi, say where you're going, and survive a little small talk on the way.
visit.summary: Took a taxi from the airport to the hotel; said where you're from.
visit.dialogue:
— Bonjour ! Taxi ?
— Bonjour. Oui, s'il vous plaît. Je vais à l'hôtel du Nord, rue de Lyon.
— D'accord. C'est votre valise ?
— Oui, merci.
— Vous venez d'où ?
— Je viens de Chicago. C'est mon premier jour à Paris.
— Bienvenue ! Voilà, nous sommes à l'hôtel. Ça fait trente euros.
— Voilà. Merci, au revoir !
— Merci. Bonne journée !
visit.translation:
— Hello! Taxi?
— Hello. Yes, please. I'm going to the Hôtel du Nord, rue de Lyon.
— All right. Is this your suitcase?
— Yes, thank you.
— Where are you from?
— I'm from Chicago. It's my first day in Paris.
— Welcome! Here we are, we're at the hotel. That's thirty euros.
— Here you go. Thanks, goodbye!
— Thank you. Have a good day!

bundle.gloss: here you go; there it is

prompts.situation: You get into a taxi at the airport. Greet the driver and tell him you're going to the Hôtel du Nord.
prompts.exampleAnswer: Bonjour ! Je vais à l'hôtel du Nord, s'il vous plaît.

prompts.situation: The driver asks where you're from. Tell him.
prompts.exampleAnswer: Je viens de Chicago.

title: Le café
brief: It's 7am, you haven't slept, and there's a café on the corner with its lights on.

visit.brief: Order a coffee at the counter. Then change your mind.
visit.summary: Ordered a coffee, switched to a café crème, added a croissant, paid.
visit.dialogue:
— Bonjour !
— Bonjour. Je voudrais un café, s'il vous plaît.
— Un café. Sur place ou à emporter ?
— Sur place. Euh… en fait, un café crème, s'il vous plaît.
— Très bien. Et avec ça ? Un croissant ?
— Oui, un croissant aussi. C'est combien ?
— Quatre euros cinquante.
— Voilà. Merci beaucoup.
— Merci à vous. Bonne journée !
visit.translation:
— Hello!
— Hello. I'd like a coffee, please.
— A coffee. For here or to go?
— For here. Uh… actually, a coffee with milk, please.
— Very good. Anything with that? A croissant?
— Yes, a croissant too. How much is it?
— Four euros fifty.
— Here you go. Thanks very much.
— Thank you. Have a good day!

prompts.situation: It's 7am, you've just landed, and you're at the counter of a café. Order a coffee.
prompts.exampleAnswer: Bonjour, je voudrais un café, s'il vous plaît.

prompts.situation: You want it to go, and you'd like to know the price.
prompts.exampleAnswer: À emporter, s'il vous plaît. C'est combien ?

title: Les présentations
brief: A friend's dinner party. Someone you've never met sits down next to you and smiles.

visit.brief: Say who you are, where you live, and ask the same back.
visit.summary: Met Claire at a dinner; exchanged names, where you live, which languages you speak.
visit.dialogue:
— Salut ! Je m'appelle Claire. Et toi, comment tu t'appelles ?
— Bonjour, je m'appelle Sam. Enchanté.
— Enchantée ! Tu es américain ?
— Oui, je suis américain. J'habite à Boston. Et toi ?
— Moi, je suis française. J'habite ici, à Lyon.
— Tu parles anglais ?
— Un peu. Et toi, tu parles bien français !
— Merci, mais je parle un petit peu seulement. J'apprends.
visit.translation:
— Hi! My name's Claire. And you, what's your name?
— Hello, my name's Sam. Pleased to meet you.
— Pleased to meet you! Are you American?
— Yes, I'm American. I live in Boston. And you?
— Me, I'm French. I live here, in Lyon.
— Do you speak English?
— A little. And you, you speak French well!
— Thanks, but I only speak a little bit. I'm learning.

prompts.situation: At a dinner, someone new says hello. Introduce yourself and say where you live.
prompts.exampleAnswer: Bonjour, je m'appelle Sam. J'habite à Boston.

prompts.situation: Now turn it around: ask about them, and whether they speak English.
prompts.exampleAnswer: Et toi ? Tu parles anglais ?

title: La boulangerie
brief: The bakery under your building. There is a queue behind you and the baker is fast.

visit.brief: Buy bread. One of the things you want has sold out.
visit.summary: Bought a baguette, two croissants and a wholemeal loaf; the seeded bread was sold out.
visit.dialogue:
— Bonjour madame !
— Bonjour. Vous désirez ?
— Je voudrais une baguette et deux croissants, s'il vous plaît.
— Voilà. Et avec ça ?
— Vous avez du pain aux céréales ?
— Non, désolée, il n'y en a plus. Mais il y a du pain complet.
— D'accord, je prends un pain complet.
— Ce sera tout ?
— Oui, c'est tout, merci.
— Ça fait six euros vingt.
visit.translation:
— Hello, madam!
— Hello. What would you like?
— I'd like a baguette and two croissants, please.
— Here you are. Anything else?
— Do you have any seeded bread?
— No, sorry, there's none left. But there's wholemeal bread.
— All right, I'll take a wholemeal loaf.
— Will that be all?
— Yes, that's all, thanks.
— That comes to six euros twenty.

prompts.situation: You're at the front of the queue in the bakery. Ask for a baguette and two croissants.
prompts.exampleAnswer: Bonjour, je voudrais une baguette et deux croissants, s'il vous plaît.

prompts.situation: The baker asks if that will be all. It is. Say so, and thank her.
prompts.exampleAnswer: Oui, c'est tout, merci.

title: Se déplacer
brief: Your phone is dead, you're somewhere in Lyon, and your train leaves in forty minutes.

visit.brief: Stop someone and ask the way. They will answer too fast.
visit.summary: Asked a passer-by for the station and the metro; had to ask him to repeat.
visit.dialogue:
— Excusez-moi, monsieur. Où est la gare, s'il vous plaît ?
— La gare ? C'est tout droit, puis à gauche.
— C'est loin ?
— Non, c'est à cinq minutes à pied. Ou vous pouvez prendre le métro.
— Où est le métro ?
— Là, à droite, en face de la banque.
— Je ne comprends pas. Vous pouvez répéter, s'il vous plaît ?
— Bien sûr. Le métro est à droite, en face de la banque.
— Ah, d'accord. Merci beaucoup, monsieur !
— De rien. Bonne journée !
visit.translation:
— Excuse me, sir. Where is the station, please?
— The station? It's straight ahead, then left.
— Is it far?
— No, it's five minutes on foot. Or you can take the metro.
— Where is the metro?
— There, on the right, opposite the bank.
— I don't understand. Can you repeat that, please?
— Of course. The metro is on the right, opposite the bank.
— Ah, okay. Thank you very much, sir!
— You're welcome. Have a good day!

prompts.situation: You're lost. Stop a passer-by politely and ask where the train station is.
prompts.exampleAnswer: Excusez-moi, où est la gare, s'il vous plaît ?

prompts.situation: He answered much too fast. Tell him you don't understand and ask him to say it again.
prompts.exampleAnswer: Je ne comprends pas. Vous pouvez répéter, s'il vous plaît ?

title: Au restaurant
brief: Evening. A small restaurant with a chalkboard menu; you and one other person are hungry.

visit.brief: Get a table, order for two, and ask for the bill at the end.
visit.summary: Dinner for two: water and red wine, chicken and fish, then the bill.
visit.dialogue:
— Bonsoir ! Une table pour deux personnes ?
— Oui, s'il vous plaît.
— Voici la carte. Vous voulez boire quelque chose ?
— Une carafe d'eau et un verre de vin rouge, s'il vous plaît.
— Très bien. Vous avez choisi ?
— Oui. Pour moi, le poulet, et pour elle, le poisson.
— Parfait.

Plus tard, le serveur revient.

— C'était bon ?
— Oui, c'était très bon, merci. L'addition, s'il vous plaît.
— Tout de suite.
visit.translation:
— Good evening! A table for two?
— Yes, please.
— Here's the menu. Would you like something to drink?
— A carafe of water and a glass of red wine, please.
— Very good. Have you chosen?
— Yes. For me, the chicken, and for her, the fish.
— Perfect.

Later, the waiter comes back.

— Was it good?
— Yes, it was very good, thanks. The bill, please.
— Right away.

prompts.situation: You walk into a restaurant in the evening with one other person. Greet the waiter and ask for a table.
prompts.exampleAnswer: Bonsoir ! Une table pour deux, s'il vous plaît.

prompts.situation: The meal is over and you're ready to leave. Ask for the bill.
prompts.exampleAnswer: L'addition, s'il vous plaît.

title: Le logement
brief: The hotel lobby, late. You have a booking, a passport, and a strong wish to lie down.

visit.brief: Check in, find out where your room is and when breakfast happens.
visit.summary: Checked in for three nights: room twelve, second floor, breakfast from seven to ten.
visit.dialogue:
— Bonsoir. J'ai une réservation au nom de Miller.
— Bonsoir, madame. Oui, une chambre pour trois nuits. Votre passeport, s'il vous plaît.
— Voilà.
— Merci. Voici la clé. C'est la chambre douze, au deuxième étage.
— Il y a un ascenseur ?
— Oui, à gauche.
— À quelle heure est le petit déjeuner ?
— De sept heures à dix heures.
— Et quel est le code du wifi ?
— C'est écrit sur la carte. Bonne soirée !
visit.translation:
— Good evening. I have a reservation under the name Miller.
— Good evening, madam. Yes, a room for three nights. Your passport, please.
— Here you go.
— Thank you. Here's the key. It's room twelve, on the second floor.
— Is there a lift?
— Yes, on the left.
— What time is breakfast?
— From seven to ten.
— And what's the wifi code?
— It's written on the card. Have a good evening!

prompts.situation: You arrive at your hotel in the evening. Greet the receptionist and say you have a reservation.
prompts.exampleAnswer: Bonsoir, j'ai une réservation au nom de Miller.

prompts.situation: Before you go up, ask what time breakfast is.
prompts.exampleAnswer: À quelle heure est le petit déjeuner ?

title: Dîner en famille
brief: Your partner's parents' front door. You are holding flowers. The door opens.

visit.brief: Meet the parents, hand over the flowers, and say the right thing about the food.
visit.summary: Met Michel and Anne, Julie's parents; brought flowers; praised the gratin and took seconds.
visit.dialogue:
— Bonsoir ! Entrez, entrez. Je suis Michel, le père de Julie.
— Bonsoir, monsieur. Enchanté. Merci pour l'invitation.
— Avec plaisir ! Voici ma femme, Anne.
— Bonsoir, madame. J'ai apporté des fleurs pour vous.
— Oh, merci, c'est très gentil ! Vous avez faim ?
— Oui, un peu. Ça sent très bon !
— À table, tout le monde !

Plus tard, à table.

— C'est délicieux, madame.
— Merci ! Vous voulez encore un peu de gratin ?
— Oui, je veux bien, merci.
visit.translation:
— Good evening! Come in, come in. I'm Michel, Julie's father.
— Good evening, sir. Pleased to meet you. Thank you for the invitation.
— With pleasure! This is my wife, Anne.
— Good evening, madam. I brought flowers for you.
— Oh, thank you, that's very kind! Are you hungry?
— Yes, a little. It smells very good!
— To the table, everyone!

Later, at the table.

— It's delicious, madam.
— Thank you! Would you like a little more gratin?
— Yes, I'd love some, thank you.

bundle.gloss: tu or vous: who gets which

prompts.situation: Your partner's father opens the door and introduces himself. Greet him politely and thank him for the invitation.
prompts.exampleAnswer: Bonsoir, monsieur. Enchanté. Merci pour l'invitation.

prompts.situation: Her mother offers you more gratin. Accept warmly, and tell her it's delicious.
prompts.exampleAnswer: Oui, je veux bien, merci. C'est délicieux !

title: La pharmacie
brief: You woke up feeling terrible. The green cross of a pharmacy is blinking across the street.

visit.brief: Tell the pharmacist what's wrong and since when.
visit.summary: Headache and sore throat since last night; got medicine to take three times a day.
visit.dialogue:
— Bonjour. Je peux vous aider ?
— Bonjour. Oui, je ne me sens pas très bien. J'ai mal à la tête et j'ai mal à la gorge.
— Vous avez de la fièvre ?
— Je ne sais pas. Peut-être un peu.
— Depuis quand ?
— Depuis hier soir.
— D'accord. Prenez ce médicament trois fois par jour, après les repas.
— Merci. Ça coûte combien ?
— Huit euros. Si ça ne va pas mieux dans trois jours, allez voir un médecin.
visit.translation:
— Hello. Can I help you?
— Hello. Yes, I don't feel very well. I have a headache and a sore throat.
— Do you have a fever?
— I don't know. Maybe a little.
— Since when?
— Since last night.
— All right. Take this medicine three times a day, after meals.
— Thanks. How much does it cost?
— Eight euros. If it's no better in three days, go and see a doctor.

bundle.gloss: my … hurts, I have a pain in

prompts.situation: You're ill and standing in a pharmacy. Tell the pharmacist your head hurts.
prompts.exampleAnswer: Bonjour. J'ai mal à la tête.

prompts.situation: She asks how long you've felt like this. It started last night.
prompts.exampleAnswer: Depuis hier soir.

title: On se voit ?
brief: Your phone buzzes. A French friend is texting you about this week.

visit.brief: Make a plan by text: when, where, and what after.
visit.summary: Agreed by text on the cinema tomorrow at half past seven, and dinner after.
visit.dialogue:
— Salut ! Tu es libre ce soir ?
— Salut ! Ce soir, non, je travaille. Mais demain, oui.
— Super. On va au cinéma demain soir ?
— Bonne idée ! À quelle heure ?
— Le film commence à vingt heures. On se retrouve à sept heures et demie devant le cinéma ?
— Ça marche. Et après, on mange quelque chose ?
— Oui, avec plaisir. Je connais un bon restaurant à côté.
— Parfait. À demain !
— À demain !
visit.translation:
— Hi! Are you free tonight?
— Hi! Tonight, no, I'm working. But tomorrow, yes.
— Great. Shall we go to the cinema tomorrow evening?
— Good idea! What time?
— The film starts at eight. Shall we meet at half past seven in front of the cinema?
— That works. And afterwards, shall we eat something?
— Yes, with pleasure. I know a good restaurant nearby.
— Perfect. See you tomorrow!
— See you tomorrow!

prompts.situation: Text a friend (you say tu to each other) and ask if they're free tonight.
prompts.exampleAnswer: Salut ! Tu es libre ce soir ?

prompts.situation: They can't tonight but suggest the cinema tomorrow. Say it's a good idea and ask what time.
prompts.exampleAnswer: Bonne idée ! À quelle heure ?

title: Ma journée
brief: Evening, back at the flat. Someone you like asks what you got up to today.

visit.brief: Say what you did today. This is where the past tense comes in.
visit.summary: Told her about the museum, lunch by the Seine and a long walk; she worked all day.
visit.dialogue:
— Alors, qu'est-ce que tu as fait aujourd'hui ?
— Ce matin, j'ai visité le musée d'Orsay. C'était magnifique.
— Et cet après-midi ?
— J'ai mangé au bord de la Seine, puis j'ai marché jusqu'à Notre-Dame.
— Tu as pris le métro ?
— Non, je suis allé à pied. J'aime bien marcher ! Et toi, tu as passé une bonne journée ?
— Moi, j'ai travaillé toute la journée. Je suis fatiguée.
— Alors ce soir, on reste à la maison ?
— Oui, bonne idée.
visit.translation:
— So, what did you do today?
— This morning, I visited the Musée d'Orsay. It was magnificent.
— And this afternoon?
— I ate by the Seine, then I walked to Notre-Dame.
— Did you take the metro?
— No, I went on foot. I like walking! And you, did you have a good day?
— Me, I worked all day. I'm tired.
— So tonight, shall we stay home?
— Yes, good idea.

prompts.situation: Your partner asks what you did today. You visited a museum this morning, then ate by the river.
prompts.exampleAnswer: Ce matin, j'ai visité un musée, puis j'ai mangé au bord de la Seine.

prompts.situation: Now ask her what she did today.
prompts.exampleAnswer: Et toi, qu'est-ce que tu as fait aujourd'hui ?

title: À mon avis
brief: Walking out of the cinema with a friend who always has opinions, and wants yours.

visit.brief: Say what you thought, agree a little, disagree a little.
visit.summary: Discussed the film: you liked the story, she found it too long; both like the actress.
visit.dialogue:
— Alors, tu as aimé le film ?
— Oui, j'ai bien aimé. Je pense que l'histoire est intéressante. Et toi ?
— Moi, pas vraiment. À mon avis, c'est trop long.
— C'est vrai, c'est un peu long. Mais j'aime beaucoup l'actrice.
— Je suis d'accord, elle est excellente. Pourtant, je préfère son premier film.
— Pourquoi ?
— Parce que c'est plus drôle.
— Tu as raison. On regarde ça ce week-end ?
visit.translation:
— So, did you like the film?
— Yes, I quite liked it. I think the story is interesting. And you?
— Me, not really. In my opinion, it's too long.
— That's true, it's a bit long. But I really like the actress.
— I agree, she's excellent. Still, I prefer her first film.
— Why?
— Because it's funnier.
— You're right. Shall we watch that this weekend?

prompts.situation: A friend asks if you liked the film. You did: say you think the story is interesting.
prompts.exampleAnswer: Oui, j'ai bien aimé. Je pense que l'histoire est intéressante.

prompts.situation: She says it was too long. Agree that it's true, but add that you really like the actress.
prompts.exampleAnswer: C'est vrai, c'est un peu long. Mais j'aime beaucoup l'actrice.
